description: Single storey rear extension and extension of first floor existing roof terrace.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location PlanBlock Plan3062/1A3062/2A3062/3A3062/4A3062/5A3062/6AReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be in materials to match the existing building or carried out in materials as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The area of the flat roof outside of the area marked terrace as shown on submitted drawing No. 3062/4A shall not be used for any recreational purpose and access shall only be for the purposes of the maintenance of the property or means of emergency escape. Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining properties.

That the terrace screening as shown on drawing Nos. 3062/4A and 3062/5A shall be installed and thereafter retained in perpetuity unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining properties.

Prior to above ground works details of a 1.8m privacy screen on the side with No. 110, serving the proposed raised patio shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The privacy screening shall be installed in accordance with the details approved before the first use of the development and be maintained in perpetuity.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of the adjoining neighbour.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of the on and off site trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a tree survey, a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include: 1. location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained     trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012); 2. methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing     hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs; 3. site specific methodology for the foundation installation and all associated works with RPAs; 4. details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs; 5. a full specification for the construction of all paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the    existing layout of hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement    system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and    extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP; 6. detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig    surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with    prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses; 7. a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs; 8. a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both    demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the    fencing and extent of ground protection; 9. a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);10. details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of      equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;11.  methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping. The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details. Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The foundations for the development shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the guidelines set out in NHBC 4.2 (Building near Trees).Reason: To ensure that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that trees of high amenity value and public benefit / protected trees will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
